14.translate_note: root cause found: safety inference's DivisorIsSafe rejected any divisor containing a RelIDTerm regardless of whether it denoted a genuine row-level variable needing grounding or a bare reference to a 0-ary relation (e.g. all_revenue in 100 * promo_revenue / all_revenue) -- VariablesVisitor only populates a RelIDTerm's `variables` for an actual variable, so an id with none is safe to divide by (a deterministic value computed once, not per row). Fixed by checking `variables` instead of node type, and giving TermToDomain a case for a bare 0-ary relation reference (DefinedDomain). Also generalized to allow dividing by a variable whose bound is itself functionally-determined (an aggregate-application witness, e.g. Q8's market_share) while still rejecting one bound to a raw multi-row EDB/IDB column (preserving SafetyTest.CompositionalDivByVariableFails's original guarantee) -- see Q8.

2.translate_note: root cause found: RelContextBuilder::AddVar silently refuses to register a variable whose name collides with a known relation (`if (idb_.count(var) || edb_.count(var)) return;`) — Q2's supplycost(part, supplier, suppcost) binds "part"/"supplier" as genuine variables, but since those names are also EDB relations, VariablesVisitor never marks them free, so the conjunction body never projects them as columns. Visit(RelFormulaAbstraction) then blindly built Column(vb->id, formula_source) assuming every binding was projected by name; when the wrapping subquery got flattened away, the never-actually-existing "part"/"supplier" column references were left dangling (ScopeValidator: column references an alias not visible here). Fixed by porting Visit(RelExprAbstraction)'s existing recovery pattern (FindColumnForVariableViaBaseTable, tracing which base-table argument position a binding was actually bound to) to Visit(RelFormulaAbstraction), scoped to a RelConjunction formula to avoid reaching into a RelUniversal's deliberately-unmergeable nested subquery (TranslationTest.WeirdEdgeCase1 regressed and required this scoping, same reasoning as Round 7's Visit(RelExistential) fix).

5.compare_local_note: verified by hand against SF0.01 real data (2026-09-15): all 5 nation rows match the reference exactly (revenue values match to the cent, e.g. VIETNAM 1000926.6999, CHINA 740210.7570, JAPAN 660651.2425, INDONESIA 566379.5276, INDIA 422874.6844).
5.translate_note: root cause found: CollectRelIdTermNames/ComputeAggregateGroupKeys treated bare 0-ary-relation references used directly as comparison operands (e.g. lower/upper in `lower <= o_orderdate[o] < upper`) the same as genuine free variables, leaking a nested translation's own alias into the caller's group-by/binding-column list as an out-of-scope column — same root cause as Q7. Fixed by distinguishing the two via actual usage (an id seen as an application argument, e.g. `l_shipdate[o,num]`'s o/num, is a real variable; one never used that way is a bare relation reference) rather than by free_variables, which is not reliably populated for every nested sub-expression scope.

7.compare_local_note: verified by hand against SF0.01 real data (2026-09-15): exact match with the reference, all 4 rows (FRANCE/GERMANY and GERMANY/FRANCE, 1995 and 1996, revenue matching to the cent). Was blocked by the dangling-alias bug (see translate_note), then by a separate tautological self-join in shipment_volume (T4.num = T4.num AND T4.o = T4.o where a real join to the date_year-lifted l_shipdate table should be, plus an orphaned unused l_revenue table) that turned SELECT * FROM result into a cartesian product hanging on real data — both now fixed. Root cause of the second bug: ExtractScalarSqlTerm (shared by every builtin call, e.g. date_year[...]) discarded a wrapped partial application's own key/binding columns (e.g. o/num in l_shipdate[o,num]), keeping only its value term; downstream code resolving a shared free variable's column name on that builtin's translated select found nothing and silently guessed the bare variable name, which the optimizer's dangling-column rebinder then "fixed" into a self-referential tautology instead of a real join. Fixed in two parts: (1) ExtractScalarSqlTerm now also returns the discarded key columns, and RelBuiltinDateExpr's ExtractYear projects them alongside its own value column, following the existing "key columns first, value last" convention so they propagate upward through the normal channels; (2) where that still isn't enough (an intermediate merge step can still fail to carry the name through), Visit(RelCondition)/Visit(RelExistential) recover a missing free variable's column by tracing back to the base table that actually produced it (FindColumnForVariableViaBaseTable), scoped to a RelConjunction formula and to sources not marked inhibit_subquery_flatten to avoid reaching into a scope the flattener deliberately keeps isolated (verified via TranslationTest.NestedQuantifiers2, a RelUniversal case that regressed and required this scoping). A third, unrelated bug found along the way: Visit(RelComparison) built a domain-grounding source for every SmallCover bound regardless of relevance to that comparison's own free variables, leaving an orphaned unconstrained l_extendedprice source in Q7's case — fixed by skipping bounds that don't intersect node->free_variables.
7.translate_note: root cause found: CollectRelIdTermNames/ComputeAggregateGroupKeys treated bare 0-ary-relation references used directly as comparison operands (e.g. lower/upper in `lower <= l_shipdate[o,num] < upper`) the same as genuine free variables, leaking a nested translation's own alias into the caller's group-by/binding-column list as an out-of-scope column — same root cause as Q5. Fixed by distinguishing the two via actual usage (an id seen as an application argument is a real variable; one never used that way is a bare relation reference) rather than by free_variables, which is not reliably populated for every nested sub-expression scope.

8.translate_note: market_share[o_year]'s divisor (sum[lineitem_vol_all[o_year]]) is a full aggregate expression, not a bare 0-ary relation reference like Q14's all_revenue — TermRewriter lifts it into an aggregate-application witness variable (e.g. _x17) grounded via ComputeRelAbsApplicationSafety's IntensionalDomain/Projection bound. Fixed alongside Q14 by having DivisorIsSafe recognize this shape (DomainIsFunctionallyDetermined: for whatever already-bound outer variables produced it, the aggregate evaluates to exactly one row) as safe to divide by, distinct from and still rejecting a variable bound to a raw multi-row EDB/IDB column.
